entries.title: I Chronicles 25:1
segments: Asaph; he was descended from Gershon or Gershom, the eldest son of Levi.
Heman; the grandson of Samuel, and a descendant of Kohath, Levi's second son.
Jeduthun; supposed to be the same as Ethan, a descendant of Merari, the youngest of Levi's sons.

Jeduthun signifies "praising," or "celebrating," and seems to have been a name given him from his office. 
 
  Prophesy with harps--cymbals; they not only sung inspired songs, accompanying them with instrumental music, but themselves received, at times at least, the spirit of prophecy.  To Asaph, twelve psalms--
--are all in probability to be ascribed. Heman is called "the king's seer,"
; and both Heman and Ethan (Jeduthun) were celebrated for their wisdom.
To praise God is one of the noblest services in which men can engage; and where it is done from the heart it is acceptable to God, and raises the affections to him.

entries.title: I Chronicles 25:5
segments:
Lift up the horn; blow it loudly. 
 
Children are the gift of God; and whether they be sons or daughters, the great object of parents should be to train them up for his service.

entries.title: I Chronicles 25:7
segments: All that were cunning; these two hundred and eighty-eight--twelve times twenty-four--were the teachers mentioned in the following verse. The remainder of the four thousand were the scholars.

entries.title: I Chronicles 25:8
segments: Ward; here put for a course of singers.
